svg.title: Scene 89: The life of a tag: a guardrail and a safety check at every stage
svg.desc: Four frames. 1, seven stages in order: issue and provision, register, discover, locate, share, revoke, retire. 2, a security guardrail for each stage: keys made in secure hardware and signed firmware; one account with two-factor sign-in; rotating identifiers and no pairing to overhear; end-to-end encrypted reports opened only on the owner’s devices; explicit, limited invitations; stopping sharing and removing devices; removing the tag from the account before it changes hands. 3, a human-safety checkpoint for each: alerts on by design; a tag linked to someone else cannot be quietly added; separated tags become detectable; people carrying an unknown tag can be alerted and can read its serial number; review who can see you; plan before changing sharing, because it can alert an abuser; treat a second-hand tag still linked to someone as a warning sign. 4, a closing note that disabling a tracker can alert whoever placed it.
svg.text: The life of a tag: a
Seven stages. At each one, something protects the
data and something protects the person.

text.tspan: Safety first. Disabling a tracker can alert
whoever placed it, and so can changing who it is
Decide with someone you trust, a support service or the
platform’s safety guide. Steps here follow Apple’s
documented design; other ecosystems differ in detail
